answer: A farm that floods the queue early as a result gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Because the cedar ordering is published with the oasis batch, the crystal audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 35% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Honest users pay that once, farms 31 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
